purpose: Source contract for the current Orange Plan Academy Advanced Library. Every lesson is conditional and returns to a Core planning area.

lessons.title: What changes across the 1,000 test runs?
lessons.gate: The learner wants to inspect the model beneath confidence or decide whether the built-in model is reasonable.
lessons.question: What stays fixed, what changes across the 1,000 test runs, and why is the comparison useful?
lessons.decision: Whether the built-in model is the Baseline and which one alternate assumption is worth testing.
lessons.example: The same age-55 plan measures 94.6% at 3% inflation and 91.6% at 4% inflation using comparable paths.

lessons.title: When should a holding use its own return or income assumptions?
lessons.gate: One holding would be modeled incorrectly by its broad asset-class default.
lessons.question: Does this holding genuinely behave differently from the broad class Orange Plan is using?
lessons.decision: Which holdings receive a documented override and which remain on the Plan default.
lessons.example: FBTC is labeled ETF but should follow Bitcoin assumptions rather than a broad stock assumption.
holds: final UI label for holding projection overrides

lessons.title: What does a Bitcoin-backed loan change, and how does LTV move?
lessons.gate: A Bitcoin-backed loan already exists or is actively being compared.
lessons.question: What changes when Bitcoin becomes collateral, and how far can price fall before the lender controls the outcome?
lessons.decision: Whether the loan belongs in the plan and the maximum starting LTV under the actual agreement.
lessons.example: $30,000 borrowed against 1.50 BTC starts at 20% LTV; illustrative 65% and 80% thresholds map to $30,769 and $25,000 BTC.

lessons.title: Build the top-up, repayment, and liquidation survival plan
lessons.gate: The loan remains under consideration after the LTV lesson.
lessons.question: What will the household do at each risk line, what resources are actually available, and how does the loan end?
lessons.decision: The action ladder, finite top-up/paydown resources, repayment source, hard exit, and estate handoff.
lessons.example: At the illustrative 65% line, restoring 50% LTV requires about 0.45 BTC or $6,923 cash; a 0.50 BTC reserve cannot survive every lower price.
lessons.returnToCore: Debt, custody exposure, Retirement Income, and estate handoff

lessons.title: Compare selling Bitcoin with borrowing against it
lessons.gate: The household has one real cash need and is choosing between a sale and a loan.
lessons.question: Which cost and risk is the household choosing in exchange for the same cash?
lessons.decision: Sell, borrow, or use another funding source after comparing the full plan.
lessons.example: $30,000 need funded by selling 0.30 BTC with $10,000 basis versus borrowing $30,000 against 1.50 BTC at 20% LTV.
lessons.returnToCore: Retirement Income or life-event funding source

lessons.title: Evaluate the lender and write the exit rules
lessons.gate: A specific lender remains under consideration.
lessons.question: What legal, custody, liquidation, and operating structure is the household accepting, and how does it leave?
lessons.decision: Whether the provider is acceptable and the written events that reduce or close the loan.
lessons.example: A lower-rate full-custody/full-liquidation provider versus a higher-rate provider with different collateral-control and partial-liquidation terms.
lessons.returnToCore: Debt ceiling, Reserve, Protect, and estate handoff

lessons.title: Finish cost-basis reconstruction and execute lot identification
lessons.gate: Taxable Bitcoin has missing history or a disposition is expected.
lessons.question: How do we finish the missing record and make the modeled lot match the real documented sale?
lessons.decision: Which records must be reconstructed and who owns the final identification/evidence process.
lessons.example: The demo has 1.25 BTC complete, 0.40 BTC reconstructed from purchases and an old sale, and 0.10 BTC still unresolved.
lessons.returnToCore: Tax roadmap and Retirement Income sale estimate

lessons.title: Size a Roth conversion without filling the wrong bucket
lessons.gate: The household has meaningful traditional money and a lower-income window worth comparing.
lessons.question: How much income room is actually available, what else changes when we use it, and is paying tax now better?
lessons.decision: The year, conversion range, tax-payment source, and income-based limits to protect.
lessons.example: $40,000 expected ordinary income under an $80,000 planning ceiling creates $40,000 first-pass room before healthcare and tax interactions.
lessons.returnToCore: Tax strategy and retirement withdrawal phase

lessons.title: Harvest gains or losses only when the opportunity is real
lessons.gate: Supported taxable lots contain a meaningful current gain or loss and the household has a reason to realize it.
lessons.question: Does realizing this gain or loss improve the full plan after tax, basis, exposure, and execution?
lessons.decision: Whether to act now, which lot and amount, and what future purpose makes the action useful.
lessons.example: $25,000 value/$40,000 basis loss lot versus $30,000 value/$10,000 basis gain lot, each compared with doing nothing and a smaller action.
lessons.returnToCore: One current Tax action or deliberate pass

lessons.title: Evaluate state relocation as a life decision, not a tax trick
lessons.gate: A move is genuine or a material taxable event makes residence important.
lessons.question: After tax, housing, insurance, work, family, residency, and time, does the move improve the life and plan?
lessons.decision: Whether the move is real enough to model and which residency/tax questions require confirmation.
lessons.example: Illustrative $20,000 state-tax difference on a $500,000 gain versus $60,000 of added living costs over three years.
lessons.returnToCore: Baseline state and life events after commitment

lessons.title: Map the account-access Bridge before 59½
lessons.gate: Retirement begins before the household can explain which accounts fund each early year.
lessons.question: Which dollars are genuinely available in each year, what tax or penalty applies, and what is the backup source?
lessons.decision: The year-by-year primary/backup access map and first shortfall.
lessons.example: The $101,948 first retirement-year draw is mapped across taxable Bridge, possible current-employer-plan access, Roth basis, and qualified HSA sources.

lessons.title: Model pre-Medicare healthcare and income interactions
lessons.gate: Retirement begins before Medicare without durable employer/spouse coverage.
lessons.question: Which coverage will the household use, what is the full cost, and how do withdrawals, gains, and conversions change it?
lessons.decision: First-year coverage path, all-in cost, income range, funding source, and Medicare transition.
lessons.example: Illustrative $12,000 net premium plus $6,000 out-of-pocket cost, with a proposed conversion raising the quote by $5,000.
lessons.returnToCore: Retirement spending, Bridge, and Tax question

lessons.title: Test account access, tax, and healthcare together
lessons.gate: Funding sources or Marketplace income make the withdrawal choice affect healthcare cost.
lessons.question: Which mix supplies the cash, preserves coverage, and improves the long-term plan without draining the Bridge?
lessons.decision: The annual funding range, income line to protect, tax source, and backup account.
lessons.example: Three paths fund the same $100,000 but create illustrative $8,000, $13,000, and $15,000 net premiums and different Bridge/tax results.
lessons.returnToCore: First Retirement Income phase and alternate Scenario

lessons.title: Decide whether a passphrase solves a real problem
lessons.gate: A tested single-signature setup still has a named privacy, discovery, or access-control problem.
lessons.question: What exact failure does the passphrase solve, and can the family recover both components for decades?
lessons.decision: Whether to add a passphrase and how the two components are separated, backed up, and tested.
lessons.example: Discovered backup words no longer expose the main wallet, but a dead owner and missing passphrase permanently lock out the family.
lessons.returnToCore: Family Custody Map and single-point-of-failure review

lessons.title: Choose collaborative custody or DIY multisig
lessons.gate: One-key risk is unacceptable and the household can maintain a multi-key wallet.
lessons.question: Who holds keys/configuration, who helps recovery, and can the family act when one person, key, or provider is unavailable?
lessons.decision: Tested single signature, collaborative 2-of-3, or DIY 2-of-3 based on family capability and independent recovery.
lessons.example: Alex can build DIY multisig, but Jordan's ability to recover without Alex is the deciding factor between DIY, collaborative, and staying simpler.
lessons.returnToCore: Custody level, failure map, people, and estate handoff

lessons.title: Migrate, operate, and prove recovery safely
lessons.gate: The household is changing wallets, adding a passphrase, moving to multisig, replacing a key, or taking over an advanced wallet.
lessons.question: How do we prove the destination, move the balance without one irreversible leap, and leave a tested family process?
lessons.decision: Destination design, staged migration, verification method, authorized combinations, and family test.
lessons.example: The 1.50 BTC balance moves through practice wallet, small live tranche, verified spend, staged transfer, and family recovery—not one transaction.
lessons.returnToCore: Protect, estate handoff, and next recovery review

lessons.section: A6 Trusts and complex estate planning
lessons.title: Does a trust solve a real problem in this plan?
lessons.gate: Core identifies a probate, incapacity, minor/special-needs, family-control, privacy, business, multi-state, creditor, or estate-tax problem.
lessons.question: What exact problem should the trust solve, and is the benefit worth the legal and operating work?
lessons.decision: Whether baseline documents are enough or counsel should compare specific trust structures for a named job.
lessons.example: Minor children, self-custodied Bitcoin, a beneficiary mismatch, and incomplete legal roles trigger attorney design advice—not an automatic trust purchase.
lessons.returnToCore: Estate roles, documents, beneficiaries, and family handoff

lessons.section: A6 Trusts and complex estate planning
lessons.title: Coordinate the trust, beneficiaries, and Bitcoin custody
lessons.gate: A trust exists or counsel recommends one.
lessons.question: Do legal ownership, provider records, tax records, and technical Bitcoin access all point to the same intended process?
lessons.decision: The final ownership/authority matrix and implementation owner for each material asset.
lessons.example: A trust says it owns 1.50 BTC and names Jordan successor trustee, while the wallet remains Alex's individual property and only Alex knows recovery.
lessons.returnToCore: Estate readiness, beneficiary review, custody map, heir letter, and contacts
